title: Differential compatibility of explicit tensor-Hom uncurrying
statement: For a scheme X and arbitrary unbounded module-sheaf cochain complexes P,L,M, let I(M) be the fixed functorial K-injective resolution and let phi:P -> Hom(L,I(M)) be a chain map. Extend the component schemeTensorHomUncurryComponent [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-model] over the total-tensor coproduct in each degree to get U_n. Then U_n followed by d_I(n,m) equals d_Tot(n,m) followed by U_m, for every pair of integer degrees n,m. The same module explicitly constructs the resulting chain map and proves its exact summand equation.

source.place: Tag 08DJ; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0A90 and 0A96; online source consulted at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08DJ and /tag/0A90

proof.text:
Test equality on every coproduct summand P^p tensor L^q, p+q=n.
For m=n+1 the total differential is d_P tensor 1 plus (-1)^p times 1 tensor d_L.
Project the chain-map equation for φ to Hom(L^q,I(M)^m). The Hom differential
projection formula gives d_I φ_p minus (-1)^p φ_p d_L, while the other side is
φ_(p+1) d_P. Apply the sheaf tensor-Hom adjunction and its symmetry to this
identity. Naturality and additivity of the adjunction identify its three terms
with evaluation followed by d_I and the two total differential summands.
Move the signed L term to the other side. The coproduct universal property
then gives the displayed equality. For m different from n+1 both complex
differentials vanish by the shape axiom. This argument applies in all integer
degrees, to unbounded complexes, and also to zero complexes and zero φ.
